A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic underfeeding of the mother results in a reduction in litter size, but that a partial compensation in litter growth is possible if the degree of underfeeding is not excessive.

the effects of dietary restriction on maternal body composition, lactational performance and pup growth are dependent on the degree of restriction and that the effects of maternal dietary restriction on pup body composition are mediated by maternal body composition.

maternal weight gain and body composition are more closely related to maternal food intake than are litter growth and composition, and the relationship between maternal and pup body composition may be mediated by maternal milk yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of chronic dietary restriction on maternal and pup body composition are dependent on the severity of restriction.
the effects of maternal diet on milk yield and pup growth are dependent upon the degree of restriction.
maternal dietary restriction has significant effects on maternal and pup body composition and on lactational performance.
